Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players of India Women can be seen in a huddle before taking the field and they seem to be in a happy mood and why not. The umpires have taken their places on the field and it will be the pairing of Samjhana Khadka and Sita Magar to open the innings for Nepal Women. Renuka Singh will begin proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, for Nepal Women to qualify, they have to chase down 179 in 10.2 overs or less. If they do that, they will qualify along with Pakistan Women, knocking India Women out. Anything else other than this will take the two Asian giants into the semis. Stay tuned as the exciting run chase is up next.

Dayalan Hemalatha is down for a quick chat. She says she liked the challenge as they practiced so that they could play at any position at any time. She has a feeling that the pitch is really slow. She ends up saying that they will go all out to win this match and she is feeling pretty confident about India's bowling unit.

India Women on the other hand were in prime position to qualify for the semifinals with 2 wins out of 2 so far and only needed to avoid a heavy defeat. They did tinker with the squad a bit and also with the batting lineup. The change up the order was a positive one as Dayalan Hemalatha managed to muster up some morale-boosting runs and put on a huge stand of 122 runs with Shafali Verma before getting out on 47. Verma too fell soon after in the 80s and India had to rebuild. Sajeevan Sajana failed to make much of an impact against some tight bowling but Jemimah Rodrigues and her inventiveness proved vital in the death overs as Jemimah struck 28 runs off 15 balls to get India close to the 180-run mark, still, much lower than they would have expected with such a brilliant start.

15 off the final over and 43 runs in the last four overs has seen India Women put on a pretty solid total of 178/3 on the board. At the beginning of this contest, Nepal Women had an outside chance of making it through to the semifinals and needed a big outing in the field. However, they conceded 81 runs without picking up a wicket in the first 8 overs and in the middle overs when they did create opportunities, there were a few dropped chances. Sita Magar bowled a lovely spell through the middle overs and eventually managed to pick up a couple of wickets for just 25 runs in her four overs. Nepal Women had pulled things back it seemed but let it slip a bit at the death and those two overs from Sabnam Rai cost them dearly.

Sabnam Rai charges in and delivers it outside off. Jemimah Rodrigues slaps it to long off and take just a single. India Women have shown a good batting display with 178/3 on the board, but might have wanted 10-15 runs more.

A pretty one-sided first 10 overs and India Women have taken the bull by its horns as the duo of Shafali Verma and Dayalan Hemalatha have had it pretty easy thus far. Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires are already out in the middle and so are the players of Nepal Women. It will be a new opening pair for India Women as Dayalan Hemalatha comes out to open alongside Shafali Verma. Kabita Kunwar has been handed the new ball and she is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is pitchside. She says that the temperature is going down with a slight breeze. Adds that this pitch has been used for 5 games and has rough patches around the good length where the wrist spinners might find assistance. Mentions that chasing might be easier on this surface as the ball will come onto the bat nicely.

The skipper of Nepal Women, Indu Barma says she is happy to bowl as they have a couple of young bowling options which might prove positive for the team. She continues that they are here to give their all-out performance. She ends up saying that they have two changes in their lineup.

Smriti Mandhana, the stand-in skipper for India Women says that they will bat first. Mentions that T20 cricket has changed in recent years says that the batters are feeling optimistic and will try and take on the bowlers. Adds that even 200 is less in this format but feels that anything above 180 will be good in these conditions. Ends by mentioning that Harmanpreet Kaur and Pooja Vastrakar have been rested and Arundhati Reddy and Sajeevan Sajana come in to replace them.

Nepal Women (Playing XI) - Samjhana Khadka, Sita Magar, Kabita Kunwar, Indu Barma (C), Dolly Bhatta (In for Roma Thapa), Rubina Chhetry, Puja Mahato, Kabita Joshi, Kajal Shrestha (WK), Bindu Rawal, Sabnam Rai (In for Kritika Marasini).

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana (C), Dayalan Hemalatha, Richa Ghosh (WK), Jemimah Rodrigues, Sajeevan Sajana (In for Harmanpreet Kaur), Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Tanuja Kanwar, Renuka Singh, Arundhati Reddy (In for Pooja Vastrakar).
TOSS - Interestingly, Smriti Mandhana has walked out for the toss and not Harmanpreet Kaur. The flip of the coin does land in favor of India Women and they have elected to BAT first.

The toss is just a few minutes away but let's now take a moment to talk about the qualification scenarios from Group A a bit. Currently, India and Pakistan are both on 4 points which means if Nepal win, they will all be on the same number of points but Nepal currently have a negative net run rate. That means, for Nepal to qualify, they would have to do so by a big margin. If India make 150 or above, Nepal have to chase down the target before the 11th over. In that case, India get knocked out as their net run rate will drop below that of Pakistan and Nepal. We shall give you an accurate mark once the first innings ends.

Nepal Women started off their campaign with a confident win over United Arab Emirates Women but faced a big defeat against Pakistan Women which harmed their net run rate. Their openers struggled initially and their middle order couldn't stabilize the innings. They will have to work on getting runs on the board, especially against a strong team like India. Their bowlers didn't have much to defend and only Kabita Joshi could manage to get a wicket. They will need to work as a unit if they want a chance at qualifying. Nepal Women were in contention for a semifinal berth but with Pakistan dismantling UAE earlier in the day, even a win against the mighty Indians will not suffice as they need a miracle in terms of the net run rate. On the other hand, India will be looking to rubber-stamp their authority on the top spot in the group with a win. Stay tuned for toss and team news.

India Women look like a very balanced outfit and they come into this game on the back of two very dominating wins. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana have been consistent at the top with the likes of Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh providing a strong finish down the order. With the experience in this batting lineup, they need not worry about getting the runs on the board. The bowlers are also complementing the batters well. With economical spells, they are also getting wickets at regular intervals. This looks like a very strong side and will hope to continue their winning streak further into the competition.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. We are at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium for the final group stage match of Group A in the Women's Asia Cup. It will be India Women against Nepal Women and surprisingly it will be a first meeting between the two neighboring nations. India have all but qualified by securing a top 2 finish while it is a big game for Nepal who are at number 3 on the table just behind Pakistan Women.
... MATCH DAY ...

The last game of Group A is upon us, which sees India Women take on Nepal Women at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium. With two emphatic victories, the Women in Blue are almost assured of a spot in the semifinals. In their campaign opener against Pakistan, the bowlers set the game up for them before the batting might was on full display against the UAE. Contributions from Shafali Verma, Richa Ghosh, and Harmanpreet Kaur propelled India to their first 200-plus total in Women's T20Is. Jemimah Rodrigues and Dayalan Hemalatha will be keen to score runs with the semifinals approaching and a potential final on the horizon. On the bowling front, Renuka Singh, Pooja Vastrakar, and Deepti Sharma have delivered consistent performances as a unit. Despite losing Shreyanka Patil to a fracture in her left hand, her replacement, Tanuja Kanwer, performed admirably on debut to fill the gap. As for Nepal, after the euphoria of their first-ever win in the Women's Asia Cup, they faced a tough defeat against Pakistan in their next match. This loss impacted their net run rate, complicating their chances of qualifying for the semifinals. With Pakistan scheduled to play the UAE before Nepal face India, Indu Barma and her team will have the advantage of knowing exactly what they need to do against India to advance. If Pakistan suffer an unexpected defeat, Nepal will need only a win against India, by any margin, to secure their spot. However, if Pakistan win, Nepal will need a significant victory against India to surpass either India or Pakistan in NRR, making their task considerably more challenging. The batting will need to perform at its best, with significant responsibility falling on Samjhana Khadka, Sita Magar, Rubina Chhetry, and captain Indu Barma. Sita, Chhetry, and Barma will also be key with the ball, and their performances as all-rounders will be critical to Nepal's success. Can Nepal conjure a spirited effort and pose a tough challenge to the defending champions? Or will it be yet another smooth ride for India? We shall find out.
